title: 7-round AES-192 impossible-differential key recovery, improved Phan construction

target.description: 7 rounds of standard AES-192 with initial AddRoundKey and final MixColumns omitted. The source reports complete master-key recovery, using impossible-differential subkey elimination followed by key-schedule completion or trial encryption.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: chosen-plaintext structures with a varying inverse-shifted column and fixed other bytes; compatible pairs are selected after encryption
assumptions: Uses the four-round impossible differential of Proposition 1 with input/output extension and early rejection of wrong key guesses.

Thirteen subkey bytes are guessed/derived, 80 bits guessed in the early-abort stage, and remaining master-key material is exhaustively completed. Page 287 reduces data by 2^0.8 while retaining the headline 2^139.2 estimate; memory-access filtering is also separately discussed.

time.note: Headline 2^139.2 seven-round AES-192 encryptions is preserved. The body prices the early stage as 2^142 one-round encryptions (142−log2(7)≈139.193), and candidate-table elimination separately as 2^143 memory accesses. No universal memory-access/encryption conversion is stated. Final data reduction by 2^0.8 is said to reduce work similarly but the final repeated headline remains 139.2; no 138.4 endpoint is fabricated.

data.note: Final source-reported chosen-plaintext budget for this instance and endpoint; distinct from intermediate pre-optimization counts.

memory.note: Section 4.1 p.287 estimates 2^65 bytes using per-80-bit-guess processing.

preprocessing.note: Appendix A precomputes 2^42 (difference,value) pairs, corresponding to 2^32 possible four-byte values and 2^10 one-active-byte alternatives, then sorts by difference. These are native table cardinality and iteration counts, not a reported complete setup-time total. Section 4.1 explicitly invokes the method.

success.description: No numerical finite-budget full-master-key success is established for this exact endpoint. The 2^-152.7 survival figure is explicitly referred to the earlier Phan full-data procedure and is not transferred to the reduced-data endpoint. The source trades data for more surviving104-bit guesses and residual96-bit exhaustive work; expected survivor limits do not quantify actual key recovery.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.

components.description: PDF6 Proposition1 and the source elimination rule: a true hypothesis cannot satisfy both conditions of the impossible differential and is not discarded by that mathematical contradiction. This is a local retention relation, not a finite-budget uniqueness or residual-search success rate.

PDF6–7: Step2 retains ciphertext pairs with eight designated zero-difference bytes. Source 2^123 candidate pairs become an expected2^59 pairs at the original 2^92-data analysis; the local 64-bit sieve is not a post-reduction survivor count.

PDF8–9: a deduced k5 column agrees with the byte already known through the AES192 schedule with source probability2^-8. The final2^91.2-data point keeps this local consistency test, not the earlier full-budget wrong-subkey expectation.
